title: Update from inside the app, and quick voice notes
thisBuild: Update button: when a newer build is on GitHub, a teal bar under the top bar says so. Tap Update: the app downloads it, saves your mess and hands it to Android. No browser, no Downloads folder. Settings has Check for updates too.

The first Update sends you to Android's Allow from this source switch for Mess Machine. Turn it on once and come back. After that Android may install without asking at all; if it asks, it is one Install tap.
Android closes the app while it swaps in the new build. A notice then says it updated: tap it to open.

Quick notes (note #20): tap the bug, talk, tap the bug again. The note stays on the phone with what was on screen and your last taps from that moment. Keep and Drop sit on the red bar while it listens. Start with "wishlist" or "feature" to pick the kind.
Notes for Claude (to write, send and read replies) moved into the ☰ menu, which shows how many notes are waiting. Send all sends them in one go.
watch: This build is the last one you install the old way. The next build should show the teal Update bar: tap it and tell me whether Android asked you anything.
Talk a long note with a few pauses: does it keep everything you said, or drop words at the pauses?
Music playing loud while you talk: does it still hear you?
limits: Android can keep listening only in short runs, so the app restarts it at each pause. Some phones beep at each restart.
The app cannot reopen itself after an update; the notice is one tap. Without notification permission there is no notice, so open it from the home screen.
Notes 21 and 22 (how controls turn on and open, and icons from your art) are proposals, not in this build.
I cannot hear the app or try Android's installer on your phone: the first real in-app update is the test.
